newsitem.title: CHINA: China says U.S. meddling in China over HK.
newsitem.headline: China says U.S. meddling in China over HK.

text.p: Beijing lashed out at the United States on Friday, accusing it of meddling in China's internal affairs over the return of Hong Kong to Chinese sovereignty this year.

"The U.S. State Department's U.S.-Hong Kong policy act report for 1997 is yet another example of the U.S. attempt to lay a finger on the Hong Kong issue and meddle with China's internal affairs," the Xinhua news agency quoted Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang as saying.

The State Department report, issued earlier this month, cited significant positive developments in Hong Kong but said China had approached the handover with some "disturbing" acts reversing gains in freedoms and civil liberties.

Shen said the report was issued in "woeful ignorance" of the situation of Hong Kong's return to China and said it was confused about Beijing's sincerity to implement the "one country, two systems" principle guiding Hong Kong's return.
Under that formula, Hong Kong's systems will remain unchanged for 50 years after the handover of the British colony at midnight on June 30.
"The report... made irrational accusations against the necessary measures that the Chinese government has adopted to safeguard a smooth return of the territory," Shen said.
"The whole situation of a smooth return of the territory and transfer of power has already been set," Shen said.

The annual State Department report portrays Hong Kong as a politically fragile society and makes clear Washington does not welcome such acts as the setting up of a China-sponsored provisional legislature and Beijing's plan to dismantle certain civil liberties.
However, Shen warned Washington that it should proceed from the overall situation in Sino-U.S. ties and act in its own interests.

Washington should "do more things that are beneficial to the territory's smooth transfer and long-term prosperity and stability, instead of making irresponsible comments about and pointing fingers at the Hong Kong issue", Shen said.
The White House said on Thursday that it was "fundamentally important" that Hong Kong residents continue to enjoy the freedoms they now have when China takes over the British colony.

Spokesman Mike McCurry was commenting on Wednesday's proposal by Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa to curtail protests and foreign funding for political parties in Hong Kong after it reverts to Chinese rule on July 1.
Tung, Hong Kong's chief executive-designate, launched the proposed curbs on Wednesday for a three-week public consultation process.
His proposals would require demonstrators to get police permission before taking to the streets and bar local groups from having ties with foreign political organisations.
